name: conditioning_recovery
description: Half-finished causal study: conditioning vs predictive loss as predictors of affine recovery. Sprint frozen; P1 and P2 resolved positive; EXP-003 is open on P3 (the handoff point); one idea backlogged.

steps.note: Level 0/1: long-term agenda and the project question.

args.--question: When can a learned representation support stable and reusable option discovery?
args.--agenda: Continual option learning: construct, retain, adapt, and retire reusable temporal abstractions for changing tasks.
args.--minimum: A self-contained technical chapter with one formal separation and one validated diagnostic.

steps.note: The claim graph is the engine: init, then author the design with add-*.

args.--claim: Across controlled excitation levels, log condition number predicts affine recovery error more reliably than predictive loss.

steps.note: Intervention structure: excitation drives both candidate predictors.
The core asserted edge: conditioning tracks recovery.
The load-bearing absence assumption of the whole claim.

args.--justification: Predictive loss is taken to be a downstream symptom of excitation, not an independent cause of recovery error.

steps.note: P1: does conditioning track recovery at all?
P2: is the rival predictor inert once excitation is conditioned on?

args.--prereg: |partial rho| < 0.2; failure to reject is not evidence of absence and is reported as such

steps.note: P3: does conditioning beat the rival on held-out prediction?

args.--metric: held-out predictive R2, K vs L, matched sample size
args.--prereg: K beats L on >= 4 of 5 seeds

steps.note: Pre-registered verdicts: the map is frozen before any result exists.

args.--note: If conditioning does not track recovery at all, the comparison against predictive loss is moot.
Predictive loss carries independent signal, so conditioning cannot be claimed as the mechanism. The association survives; the causal reading does not.
Conditioning tracks recovery but does not beat the rival predictor. The claim drops its comparative clause.
Scope is the tested excitation range only; extrapolation beyond it is a separate claim.

steps.note: Design complete and structurally sound; ready frontier is [P1].
Freeze the claim and the design hash; from here the design must not drift.

args.--claim: Across controlled excitation levels, log condition number predicts affine recovery error more reliably than predictive loss.
args.--artifact: A four-page note, results.csv, and one three-panel main figure.

steps.note: New ideas go to the backlog by default.

args.--idea: Try a variational identifiability objective for the representation.
args.--reason: Does not test the current frozen claim; it changes the representation family.

steps.note: EXP-001 on P1: the only ready probe at freeze time.

args.--question: Does condition number predict affine recovery across excitation levels?
args.--hypothesis: Rank correlation is positive and stable across seeds.
args.--measurement: Spearman correlation between log condition number and recovery error.
args.--kill: Stop using this quantity if correlation remains near zero across 30 instances and 5 seeds.

steps.note: P1 set to positive; the map stays open and the frontier advances to P2.

args.--conclusion: Conditioning tracks recovery within the tested excitation range.

steps.note: EXP-002 on P2: admitted only because P1 is positive.

args.--question: Does predictive loss carry signal beyond excitation?
args.--hypothesis: Predictive loss is inert given excitation.
args.--intervention: Condition on excitation; test partial association.
args.--measurement: Partial Spearman of predictive loss vs recovery error given excitation.
args.--kill: Treat as inert if |partial rho| < 0.2 on 30 instances x 5 seeds.

steps.note: P2 set to positive: the absence assumption L->R survives a test.

args.--conclusion: Predictive loss carries no measurable signal given excitation.

steps.note: EXP-003 on P3 is OPEN — this is the handoff point. Nothing has been closed on P3 yet.

args.--question: Does conditioning beat predictive loss on held-out prediction?
args.--hypothesis: K dominates L on held-out recovery prediction at matched sample size.
args.--intervention: Train both predictors on the same runs; compare held-out R2.
args.--measurement: Held-out predictive R2, K vs L, matched sample size.
args.--kill: Stop the comparative claim if K wins on fewer than 4 of 5 seeds.

steps.comment: Replay stops here: EXP-003 is open on P3. Run `research_closure.py next` in the materialised directory to see the expected next event, or open the dashboard.
